title: Pd3P nanoparticles decorated P-doped graphene for high hydrogen storage capacity and stable hydrogen adsorption-desorption performance
material_description: PdP/P-rGO-2 | Pd3P nanoparticles (20-30 nm; SEM average ~20 nm) decorated P-doped reduced graphene oxide; Pd(OAc)2 (78 mg) and triphenylphosphine (PPh3, 25 mg; Pd:P source mass ratio 4:1) added together to an ethanol solution of thermally expanded GO (100 mg), freeze-dried and reduced at 1173 K in 10% H2-Ar; nominal Pd loading 15 wt%; XRD pure Pd3P phase
functional_groups: P-O, P-C, P-Pd (XPS P 2p); O-H, C-O, -CH2/C-H (FT-IR)
source_location: main p.1 abstract; p.4 sec. 3.1; p.6 sec. 3.3; p.7; p.10 conclusions; Figs. 2(b), 6(b), 7(d) labels; SI p.S2 Table S1 ("This work")
notes: End value of the 298 K / 4 MPa kinetic (uptake vs time) test, Figs. 2(a), 6(a), 7(c); 4 MPa is the charging pressure printed (closed Sieverts test, final pressure not printed); printed 4 MPa = 40 bar. Table S1 prints "25 C, 4 MPa", Pd loading 15. Fig. 6(c) inset prints 3.66 wt% for 293 K. Not merged with the Fig. 6(d) PCT isotherm (I1): the paper attributes 3.66 wt% to the kinetic test, and the PCT markers near 4 MPa digitize at 3.023 wt% (adsorption, 3.975 MPa) and 2.703 wt% (desorption, 3.983 MPa); so no isotherm_id. Initial (first) adsorption before the 4 cycles. Sieverts test (sec. 2.5.1): about 100 mg sample activated under vacuum (printed 1 x 10^-4 MPa = 100 Pa) at 473 K (199.85 C) for 2 h; SI step (2) evacuates the system to 0.1 Pa before H2 dosing. Instrument: "high-pressure Sievert's apparatus" (schematic Fig. S1, details in ref. [34]); no manufacturer/model and not stated home-built. "The system was calibrated with LaNi5 at room temperature"; Fig. S1 lists a drainage method to calibrate container volume; how the free volume with the sample was determined is not stated. "All the above hydrogen storage performance tests were conducted at least 3 times" is stated without results or uncertainty. BET area: N2 adsorption-desorption at 77 K (ASAP 2460), Fig. 5(c) and p.5-6 text; BET P/P0 range not stated. total_pore_volume is the Fig. 5(c) "Pore Volume" (the text calls the PdP/P-rGO-2 value a "microporous volume"; a ~1 cm3/g micropore volume is inconsistent with a ~290 m2/g type-IV isotherm, so recorded as total; method unstated). Text gives "an average pore radius of about 2.8 nm" for all three samples while the PSD inset axis is pore width; average_pore_diameter left empty. Pd loading 15 wt% is nominal. GO purchased (Angxing, >=99.0%); rGO made by the authors by thermal reduction. Basis not named; volumetric default gives excess. wt% convention not defined, no paired units.
